chunks: Or do you demand any wages from them so that they are burdened with expense?

key_terms.أَمْ: Or (conjunction used for alternative or clarification)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'burdened with expense' in Surah At-Tur?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Muddaththir, this verse refutes the Meccan polytheists' claim that Muhammad (peace be upon him) preached for worldly gain by asserting that any such demand would impose a crushing financial debt (maghram) on the people. Shia exegesis highlights this as a confirmation of the Prophet's sincerity and the divine origin of his message, distinguishing him from those who sought material profit, thereby validating the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt who also sought no worldly wage.
